content:
While iOS 27 is clearly the focus of preview software, Apple is still preparing its next iPhone system update, iOS 26.6. Apple has released the fifth developer beta of iOS 26.6. The iOS 26.6 beta has been in testing since late May this year.

iOS 26.6 Features and Changes

So far, we've found two notable changes in the iOS 26.6 beta.

First, the limit on the number of contacts that can be blocked has been adjusted. Second, it appears a brand-new iPhone anti-theft feature is in development.

This update may also lay the groundwork for Spotlight indexing on iPhone and iPad, to be used by Siri AI in iOS 27.

Given that everyone's focus has shifted to iOS 27, we don't expect any other major new features or changes.

Apple's next major system update will be officially released to users in September, and Apple will continue to refine iOS 27 throughout the summer.

Following last fall's release of iOS 26 and its subsequent updates, iOS 26.6 will be the next officially released version.

Last year, the first beta of iOS 18.6 was released after the first beta of iOS 26. This means that the progress of iOS 26.6 is slightly ahead of Apple's 2025 release schedule.

9to5Mac's Take

With the fifth beta of iOS 26.6 released today, iOS 26.6 is very likely to be publicly released before the end of July. We may first see a release candidate with release notes, with the official version following about a week later.

Meanwhile, iOS 27 remains the focus of the next major update. We expect the first public beta to launch as early as this week, with the fourth developer beta likely arriving next week.

iOS 27 will not be officially released outside the preview testing cycle until September. For non-testers, the version currently in use is iOS 26.5, and iOS 26.6 will accompany most users until fall.
